summary: Multi-user data isolation vulnerability in database query layer. Range queries return unfiltered data across all users. No hardcoded secrets or injection vectors detected.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Owner Filtering in getScheduledDosesInRange
vulnerabilities.description: getScheduledDosesInRange returns all scheduled doses in a date range for ALL owners. Function signature takes only (startDate, endDate) without owner parameter. Queries db.getAllFromIndex('scheduledDoses', 'by-date', ...) without filtering by owner field.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: User Victor calls getScheduledDosesInRange('2026-07-01', '2026-07-31'). Returns 150 doses: 75 for Victor + 75 for Nadia. If Victor logs these to a chart without filtering (HalfLife.tsx), he sees Nadia's injection schedule and full dose history.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add owner parameter to function signature. Filter by owner in database query layer. Example: getScheduledDosesInRange(startDate: string, endDate: string, owner: UserName)

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Owner Filtering in getDoseLogsInRange
vulnerabilities.description: getDoseLogsInRange returns all dose logs in date range for ALL owners. Retrieves db.getAllFromIndex('doseLogs', 'by-date', ...) which crosses user boundaries without filtering.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Nadia calls getDoseLogsInRange('2026-07-01', '2026-07-31'). Returns all logs including Victor's: dates, times, doses, symptoms (rated 1-10), injection sites, and notes. Complete exposure of Victor's protocol adherence and side effects.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add owner parameter. Filter before returning: logs.filter(l => l.owner === owner)

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Owner Filtering in getVials
vulnerabilities.description: getVials returns all vials for a peptide across all owners. Does not filter by owner field.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Victor calls getVials('semaglutide'). Receives [Vial A (owner=Victor, 10 doses), Vial B (owner=Nadia, 3 doses)]. Victor knows Nadia has only 3 doses left and infers her protocol nearing completion.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add owner parameter: getVials(peptideId?: string, owner?: UserName). Filter vials.filter(v => v.owner === owner)

vulnerabilities.title: No Owner Filtering in Active Levels Chart
vulnerabilities.description: HalfLife page fetches all dose logs and scheduled doses without owner filter via getScheduledDosesInRange. Does not apply filterByOwner context before charting.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Victor views HalfLife chart. Sees combined active peptide levels from both Victor's and Nadia's doses. Chart shows inflated in-system levels from both users' protocols.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Apply useViewFilter + filterByOwner(scheduled, filter) before charting. Match Calendar.tsx pattern at line 96.

vulnerabilities.title: No Owner Filtering in Symptoms Analysis
vulnerabilities.description: Symptoms page calls getScheduledDosesInRange('2000-01-01', '2999-12-31') without owner filter. Charts mixed symptom severity data from both users.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: User sees symptom-vs-titration chart mixing both users' reported symptoms. Cannot determine which nausea/fatigue reports are theirs vs. the other user's.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Apply filterByOwner to both scheduled doses and logs before rendering chart

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Compound Index on (peptideId, owner)
vulnerabilities.description: Vials index 'by-peptide' only indexes peptideId. No compound index for efficient (peptideId, owner) queries.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Query getVials('semaglutide', 'Victor') retrieves all semaglutide vials then filters in JS. Inefficient and conceptually wrong (query layer should not leak data).

vulnerabilities.title: Cloud Sync Retrieves All Records Unfiltered
vulnerabilities.description: syncNow calls db.getAll(kind) without owner filtering. Retrieves all records across all users before merging with cloud.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: If sync logic is modified or another consumer reuses db.getAll(), unfiltered multi-user data could be processed or leaked.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Filter db.getAll() results by current user's owner before passing to planMerge()

vulnerabilities.title: Supabase Anon Key in Client - Expected Design
vulnerabilities.description: VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY is in client code. This is correct - anon key is public by design. Supabase RLS policies enforce security.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: N/A - correct design IF RLS policies are configured correctly.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Verify supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql has RLS policies enforcing auth.uid() == user_id

vulnerabilities.title: Experience Content Could Be Unescaped
vulnerabilities.description: Guide tips, dosing notes, mistakes stored as strings. If rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without escaping, XSS possible.
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario:
If ExperienceGuide.tsx renders:
and tip = '', XSS fires.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Verify ExperienceGuide.tsx uses standard JSX (auto-escapes). Avoid dangerouslySetInnerHTML for user/community content.

vulnerabilities.title: No Known Vulnerable Dependencies
vulnerabilities.description: @supabase/supabase-js, idb, date-fns, recharts, lucide-react all maintained and secure.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Run npm audit. Pin versions in package-lock.json.

recommendations: PRIORITY 1: Add owner parameter to getScheduledDosesInRange, getDoseLogsInRange, getVials. Filter at database abstraction layer.
PRIORITY 1: Fix HalfLife.tsx and Symptoms.tsx to apply filterByOwner() before rendering charts (follow Calendar.tsx pattern).
PRIORITY 2: Add compound indexes: [date, owner] on scheduledDoses/doseLogs; [peptideId, owner] on vials.
PRIORITY 2: Add integration tests verifying multi-user isolation. Create Victor data, query as Nadia, assert empty/filtered results.
PRIORITY 3: Verify Supabase RLS policies enforce user isolation by user_id in records table.
PRIORITY 3: Filter db.getAll() in sync.ts by current user before merging with cloud.
PRIORITY 4: Audit dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage. Confirm experience data uses standard JSX rendering.
PRIORITY 4: Document ownership model in CLAUDE.md: every record has owner field; all queries must filter by current user; UI-level filtering insufficient.
riskJustification: Multi-user data isolation broken in database query layer. Calendar applies UI filtering; HalfLife and Symptoms do not. Users can see each other's complete dose history, symptoms, and vial inventory. Limited by threat model (1-2 trusted users per device per CLAUDE.md), but would be CRITICAL if deployed to untrusted multi-user scenarios.
completeness: Reviewed: config, schema, operations, sync, peptides, users, three pages, tests. Did not review: all 15+ components, all pages. Additional unfiltered query usages may exist elsewhere.
